newsitem.title: SPAIN: Germany's Kirch in Spanish legal wrangle.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kirch in Spanish legal wrangle.

text.p: A spokesman for media tycoon Leo Kirch said on Friday he was checking Spanish newspaper reports that the German businessman had become embroiled in allegations of tax and investment violations.
The daily newspaper El Mundo reported that Spain's High Court had charged Kirch for violations related to the purchase of a 25 percent stake in Spanish television channel Telecinco.
The spokesman for the Kirch group said it was still unclear whether investigations were going on or whether charges had already been lodged by Spain's High Court.
"It is still unclear what this is about," spokesman Johannes Schmitz said. "We must hear and check and only then can we comment."

Officials at the High Court were not available to comment due to a public holiday in Spain. On Thursday, anti-corruption prosecutors investigating the case would only confirm that they had asked that 38 people including Italian opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi be charged.
The prosecutor's office said they were investigating investments made by Berlusconi's media group Fininvest in television channel Telecinco.
In a statement, they said Fininvest had violated limits set out in Spain's private television law which says a single shareholder can only hold 25 percent in a television station.

"Fininvest illegally exceeded this limit by possessing more than 80 percent of Telecinco's capital and used companies, people and resident bank accounts in third countries to fake fictitious ownership," prosecutors said.
Fininvest and Berlusconi denied they had committed any crimes relating to their investments in Spain.

In comments made to journalists and reported by Italian agency Ansa on Thursday, Berlusconi said: "When some partners of Telecinco decided to sell their stakes, it was necessary to assign them to companies that would hold them temporarily until professional members, which would think about benefitting, not hurting the company, were found."
Berlusconi said his executives looked for partners and companies to pass on these stakes and they were eventually handed to Leo Kirch and the editorial group Correo.
Schmitz confirmed that Kirch had held a 25 percent stake in Telecinco since 1993.
Prosecutors said they were also investigating alleged tax fraud of nearly two billion pesetas ($13 million) relating to investments in Telecinco.
